maria_g: Heads-up: saw a small OOM spike on sparse-batcher after the 11:30 deploy, only on KV-heavy chat workloads.
kevin_h: can you paste logs/profile? which model, batch sizes? :thinking:
mar ia_g: reproed on rwin-7b, 8 concurrent chat reqs, each ~600 tokens avg. batching formed 10-request batches -> total_kv_bytes jumped.
kevin_h: ok show the profiler output pls
bench-bot: PROFILE SNAPSHOT (1769605201): batch_id=8242 | reqs=8 | avg_req_tokens=615 | total_input_tokens=4920 | avg_kv_per_token=640 bytes | total_kv_bytes=3.15 GB | kv_free_before=1.12 GB | kv_free_after=88 MB | p50=82ms | p95=410ms | oom=false (eviction thrash)
nina_r: that "kv_free_after" is the problem. looks like we allowed batch formation without accounting for KV working set. queue_policy is current FIFO with soft_priority.
samir_k: i think current continuous-batching token_budget_target is static (1500) which ignores per-request KV multipliers. when many long contexts join we blow past free_kv.
kevin_h: proposed heuristic: compute token_budget_target = min(global_token_cap, floor(free_kv_bytes / avg_kv_bytes_per_token)). then cap per-batch total tokens and also limit number of variable-length requests.
kevin_h: quick pseudo:
```
// run when forming a batch
free_kv = get_kv_free_bytes();
avg_kv_per_tok = estimate_avg_kv_per_token(model, seq_len_dist);
max_tokens_by_kv = floor(free_kv / avg_kv_per_tok);
batch_token_budget = min(config.global_token_cap, max(128, max_tokens_by_kv));
// also enforce max_reqs and prefer shorter reqs if kv pressure high
```
mar ia_g: would add a hysteresis: require free_kv > 300MB to allow forming multi-request batches, otherwise fall back to passthrough or single-request batches. avoids thrash.
nina_r: agree. also add graceful degradation: if batch formation would cause free_kv_after < config.kv_safe_margin (200MB) then reduce batch by dropping lowest-priority reqs from queue.
kevin_h: implemented a canary patch: set token_budget_target= min(1200, floor(free_kv/avg_kv_per_tok)), kv_safe_margin=200MB, eviction_policy=drop_shortest_latency_penalty. rolled to canary namespace.
deploy-bot: rollout started for canary (canary-10%) at 1769605340
bench-bot: CANARY RESULTS (1769605380): vs baseline -> dropped multi-req batch formation by 63% under KV-heavy traces; p95 latency +10ms for single-request cases, OOM incidents -> 0 (from 3/day).
samir_k: good tradeoff. need to be careful about throughput cost. will run overnight perf regression tests on spiking traffic.
kevin_h: we also found kernel selection matters: the int8-optimized kernel had slightly higher per-token KV metadata size due to padding -> avg_kv_per_tok increased by ~5%. adjusted estimator.
maria_g: action items:
- samir run 12h perf regression comparing throughput/cost with canary config (start 00:30 PT)
- nina add telemetry: kv_free_before/after per-batch + dropped_reqs_reason
- kevin finalize heuristic PR and add unit tests for hysteresis and drop logic
- ops: schedule rollback window if throughput regressions > 12%
kevin_h: tiny follow-up: we should avoid global blocking on get_kv_free_bytes() call in hot path; use async snapshot sampled every 50ms.
nina_r: noted. I'll add an averaged snapshot and expose in monitoring.
maria_g: thanks team. if nightly runs look good we'll push to 50% tomorrow. :thumbsup:
